column1: # B129 GOLD MANIFEST - every engine-derived artifact committed to this repo.
# One row per artifact. `just regen-golds` reads THIS FILE, not a hand-copied
# list, and `manifest_registration_tests` in tests/b129_gold_manifest.rs fails
# if docs/probes/ holds a .tsv this file does not name (or vice versa), so a
# new corpus cannot dodge the manifest by simply not being added to it.
# COLUMNS
#   artifact        path from the repo root.
#   kind            CORPUS   engine verdicts, regenerable by running a probe.
#                   SIDECAR  derived from a corpus + the probing machine, not
#                            itself a fresh engine measurement.
#                   TYPEDB   the shipped Openplanet type dump.
#                   PRIMARY  hand-transcribed engine ground truth living in a
#                            source comment, with no output file to overwrite.
#   question        THE QUESTION THIS ARTIFACT ANSWERS. Not decoration: B118
#                   and B123 each had a right output with a wrong stated
#                   reason, and a manifest carrying only artifact+generator
#                   would regenerate both correctly while preserving the false
#                   explanation forever. A regen that changes the answer
#                   without changing the question is drift; one that changes
#                   the question is a NEW ARTIFACT and wants a new row.
#   generator       exact command, or NONE (no generator exists - a finding,
#                   see below), or MANUAL (re-verified by a human).
#   engine_version  Openplanet version the artifact was last produced against,
#                   or UNKNOWN. The runner REFUSES to diff across versions
#                   silently: three engine generations (1.29.5, 1.29.9,
#                   1.29.14) are cited concurrently in this repo, so an
#                   unqualified diff reports "changed" for artifacts that
#                   merely moved generation.
#   probe_date      date last produced.
#   rows            expected data rows (excludes the `#` preamble AND the
#                   column header), or `-`.
#   diff            STRING     the artifact IS compiler message text, so a
#                              string diff is exact, not a rendered
#                              approximation. Not blind - there is no
#                              structure under it to miss.
#                   STRUCTURED parsed and compared field-wise.
#                   MANUAL     no machine diff; the runner reports UNCHECKED.
#   dependents      source sites that RESTATE this artifact's facts in prose,
#                   `;`-separated, or `-`. Regenerating an artifact updates
#                   NONE of these, so the runner lists them UNCHECKED whenever
#                   the artifact's rows change. B094's "abstract does NOT
#                   exempt" is stated in four files in four phrasings; that
#                   fan-out, not staleness of a single file, is why in-source
#                   tables stay manual.
# EVERY CORPUS NOW HAS A GENERATOR (B148). b067 and b071 shipped as orphans --
# stamped engine gold with a documented method and no script anywhere in the
# repo -- and the runner reported them as a finding on every run until scripts
# existed. `generator=NONE` remains a legal value and is still reported that
# way; it is simply currently unused.
# WHAT THE FIRST REGENERATION FOUND. b067 came back byte-identical at 1.29.14,
# so its old 1.29.5 stamp was mislabelled and no conclusion drawn from it was
# wrong. b071 came back with three WORDING-CHANGED rows and ZERO behaviour
# changes: the engine now names an assignment target as a reference, so
# `Can't implicitly convert from 'int' to 'VirtualKey'.` is today
# `... to 'VirtualKey&'.` Same verdict, different prose -- which is why the
# question column for a message-text corpus says so explicitly.
